summary.title: Staff archetypes
summary.one_liner: Staff-plus engineering roles cluster into four archetypes (Tech Lead, Architect, Solver, Right Hand), each with different work patterns and typical company conditions.
keywords: hand of the king staff engineer
takeaways: Staff-plus career ladders often hide several distinct roles behind one title; four common archetypes are Tech Lead, Architect, Solver, and Right Hand.
Tech Lead is the most common archetype, roughly one per eight engineers, and is often a first Staff-level experience.

Architect roles tend to appear in large or highly coupled companies and focus on a critical technical domain; Solver suits companies that plan around individuals; Right Hand appears around hundreds of engineers and works as an executive's extension.
Choose an archetype by considering which kinds of work energize you and which roles your company actually offers.
Tech Lead and Architect involve long-term work with the same team, while Solver and Right Hand involve bouncing between priorities with more transactional interactions.
summary.summary: Will Larson describes a taxonomy of four Staff-plus engineering archetypes drawn from conversations with engineers at many companies. For each archetype (Tech Lead, Architect, Solver, Right Hand) he explains the scope of work, how it differs from other roles, and which company conditions tend to produce it. The page also discusses how the Tech Lead role often serves as a first Staff experience, and how to reflect on which archetype fits your energy and your company's available roles. It is an essay-style guide with linked stories and a pointer to the book Staff Engineer.
